key_insight: A multi-method explainability audit found that DeBERTa-v3 explanations agree when medical categories are clear, but diverge sharply when diagnosis is semantically ambiguous.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP systems, the study shows that both predictive performance and explanation stability should be checked before trusting transformer outputs on medical text.
method: Built a zero-shot NLI classifier over the Medical Abstracts corpus using five enriched hypotheses per diagnostic category.
Compared five explanation methods: SHAP, LIME, occlusion, Input x Gradient, and Attention x Gradient.
Measured explanation agreement with the Jaccard index after standardizing explanations to top-token attributions.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used a balanced sample of 1,000 abstracts per class and showed strong accuracy in well-defined domains but weaker performance and explanation agreement under high ambiguity.
watch_item: Results may not transfer well to broad diagnostic labels because semantic overlap and attribution instability can reduce both accuracy and interpretability.
paper_title: A Comparative Explainability Framework for DeBERTa-v3 in Zero-Shot Medical Abstract Classification
